blocks.text: You can view detailed information about information associated with an identity provider (IdP) configuration, and can also edit or delete an IdP configuration.
To view the IdP configuration details:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Private Access Authentication > IdP Configuration.
The IdP Configuration page appears.
Click the name of the IdP configuration.
The IdP Configuration Details drawer opens.
In the IdP Configuration Details drawer, you can view the following:
ZPA (SP) SAML Request: Indicates if Private Access is the service provider (SP) for a Signed or Unsigned SAML request towards the IdP.
HTTP-Redirect: This field is set to Enabled if Private Access needs to send the SAML response as an HTTP redirect.

Single Sign-On URL: The URL of the IdP portal to which users are directed for authentication. If you want users to authenticate from the internet, ensure that it is publicly resolvable. Additionally, ensure that it is protected using HTTPS.

Force Authentication: This field is set to Enabled if you want users for that specific IdP to re-enter their login credentials at the time of reauthentication, regardless of any session state/cookie for SAML IdP. The default is set to Disabled.

Login Hint: When enabled, the username of the admin or user is sent in the authentication request to the IdP and can be prepopulated on the sign-in page of the external IdP. By default, Enabled is selected.

SAML Attributes for Policy: Indicates if SAML attributes are allowed from this IdP when configuring Access Policies, Client Forwarding Policies, and Timeout Policies. This setting must be enabled for Zscaler to process SAML attributes in policy rules.

Authentication Domains: The authentication domains associated to this IdP. The domains shown here are the primary and secondary authentication domains configured for your organization. A domain can only be associated to one IdP.
Import SAML Attributes: Click Import to import your SAML attributes.
SAML Attributes: Click Show Attributes to go to the SAML Attributes page.
See image.
For Service Provider SAML Metadata for User SSO, you can view the following:
Service Provider Metadata: Click Download Metadata to download the SP metadata file.
Service Provider Certificate: Click Download Certificate to download the SP certificate.
Service Provider URL: The SP URL. Click the Copy icon () to copy the URL.
Service Provider Entity ID: The SP entity ID. Click the Copy icon to copy the entity ID.
See image.
For IdP Certificate, you can view the following:
Common Name: The common name of the IdP certificate.
Serial Number: The serial number of the IdP certificate.
Created On: The creation date of the IdP certificate.
Expires On: The expiration date of the IdP certificate.
See image.
For SCIM Configuration, you can view the following:

SCIM Sync: When enabled, allows Zscaler to more quickly remove users from Private Access when a user is disabled or deleted in your user directory and to enforce policies based on SCIM attributes and SCIM groups. To complete the SCIM enablement process, see Enabling SCIM for Identity Management.
SCIM attributes for Policy: When enabled, allows SCIM attributes and SCIM groups from this IdP to be used when configuring Access Policies, Client Forwarding Policies, and Timeout Policies.
SCIM Service Provider Endpoint: The SCIM service provider endpoint. Click the Copy icon to copy the endpoint.
See image.
In the top-right of the drawer, the Actions drop-down menu contains the following actions:
Edit: Select this option to edit the IdP configuration.
Delete: Select this option to delete the IdP configuration.
See image.
